newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks seen lower on correction.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks seen lower on correction.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks are expected to open soft and move lower on Friday as the all share index continues a correction that began two days ago, brokers said.
"The correction will continue and take the index towards 700 points, but the downward momentum may be slowed as sellers start to keep out," said Shanil Perera of Lanka Securities.
There have already been signs that the downward movement was easing due to sellers returning to the sidelines, brokers said.
"The index fell two points in Thursday's second session, whereas it fell 13 points in the morning due to heavy selling," said Prasanna Chandrasekera of John Keells Stock Brokers.
Colombo stocks, which had gained over 15 percent in four weeks due to improved investor sentiment, fell for the first time in a month on Wednesday on profit-taking.

Investor sentiment was buoyed by good growth expectations, lower cost of corporate borrowings after the Central Bank cut reserve ratios and an agreement between the govenrment and opposition to work together to end the ethnic conflict.
On Thursday, the all share index closed 15.28 points down at 730.32 on turnover of 108.7 million rupees.
